facts.heading: Anxiety worsened since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this anxiety has worsened since September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Promoted to deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school in September.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: Taught Year 4 for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Worries about competence in role
facts.content: Hannah worries that people picked the wrong person for her new role and that someone will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety peaks Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxiety thoughts are mostly on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings.

facts.heading: Rehearses meetings in head
facts.content: When anxiety hits, Hannah rehearses Monday's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Worries about being judged
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say, and then what people would think if she got it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask, and what I'd say.

facts.heading: Fears being seen as incapable
facts.content: Hannah imagines people would think she is out of her depth or that they gave the job to a teacher who cannot lead.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr Hargreaves' judgment
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the email because she was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mum was a headteacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Compares self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what she thinks her mother would have done, believing she might have done it better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother is supportive but dismissive
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface, saying Hannah worries too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hides distress from mother
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are because her mother's comments make her feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: So I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Awake at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four every morning

facts.heading: Morning worries on list
facts.content: Hannah's list includes timetable changes, Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, and a worried child.
facts.evidence: Timetable changes, the Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about

facts.heading: Waking up since second week
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up like this since about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Consumes five or six coffees
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky

facts.heading: Had to leave meeting last Thursday
facts.content: Last Thursday, Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water

facts.heading: Partner Ben's view on situation
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben believes she should just enjoy the situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it

facts.heading: Feels guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben tells her to enjoy it.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone

facts.heading: Lost friends after promotion
facts.content: Hannah has lost friends at school due to her becoming a line manager.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward

facts.heading: Misses children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and her previous class.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too

facts.heading: Promotion decision was pressured
facts.content: Hannah accepted the promotion because she felt she couldn't say no to the head.
facts.evidence: I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her

facts.heading: Cried after accepting promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried

facts.heading: Fears related to promotion
facts.content: Hannah's tears were about fear and the thought of never going back to her previous role.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back

facts.heading: Last relaxed during summer holidays
facts.content: Hannah last felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays while walking in the Lakes.
facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes

facts.heading: Holiday relaxation details
facts.content: During the holidays, nobody expected anything of Hannah, and she was just walking.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking

facts.heading: Pre-term stress started
facts.content: The week before term started, Hannah felt like a wreck and could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday

facts.heading: Tracking positive events daily
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening.

facts.heading: Stopped tracking positive events
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing down positive events after about two weeks.
facts.evidence: It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped

facts.heading: Feeling of bragging while writing
facts.content: Hannah felt like she was bragging to herself when writing in the notebook.
facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.

facts.heading: Goal: Avoid feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal: Not rehearsing meetings
facts.content: Hannah's goal is to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first.

facts.heading: Goal: Sending one email
facts.content: Hannah's goal is to send only one email.
facts.evidence: Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal: Relaxing on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Emotional response to goals
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Confiding in Ben about distress
facts.content: Hannah has never told anyone how bad things are, including Ben.
facts.evidence: Not even Ben knows about the four a.m.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah finds the idea of telling Ben scary, and fears he might be hurt.
facts.evidence: Scary. He'd probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Preferred time to talk to Ben
facts.content: Hannah prefers to talk to Ben during a quiet moment, not on Sunday evening.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment. Not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too wound up.

facts.heading: Plan to talk to Ben Saturday
facts.content: Hannah plans to talk to Ben over breakfast on Saturday morning.
facts.evidence: Yes, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Revisiting evening notebook
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week.
facts.evidence: I could. I'll put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Glad she attended session
facts.content: Hannah was glad she did not cancel the session that morning.
facts.evidence: Only that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
